title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: ximage draws data raster order: first cell matrix top-left picture, row matrix scan line reading left right, page. order western reading, par(mfrow), every image format spatial data reader (GDAL, PNG, JPEG, satellite scan lines). stream pixel values order, R matrix ximage expects (note nrow number scan lines, R asks dimensions nrow,ncol image formats declare ncol,nrow). round trip back pixel stream .vector(t(m)), getting values matrix always column-major - byrow extraction, none array() . Everything else vignette demonstration two lines whole story.

title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: xtext() draws values matrix centre cell, exactly layout ximage() uses. small labelled matrix makes convention self-evident.  Cell [1, 1] (value 1) top left. Reading along top row picture reads along first row matrix: 1, 2, 3, 4. default plot space index space matrix, 0,ncol x 0,nrow y, picture ncol wide nrow tall cell 1 x 1. Note y axis: row 1 matrix top, y = 2 y = 3. Axis coordinates increase upward R plot, row indices increase downward, image. ximage pretend otherwise, simply places first row top image expects .

title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: Base image() uses different convention: rows matrix map x axis columns y axis, first column bottom. matrix:  image() effectively rotated data 90 degrees anticlockwise: see transpose, flipped. classic incantation make image() show matrix way print forgetting one half (applying twice) source whole genre plotting bugs. ximage incantation ximage(m). rasterImage(), ximage uses underneath, already follows raster order. lacks everything else: start plot, map numeric values palette, handle missing values. ximage raster-order rasterImage() limitations removed.
code: op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) image(m, main = "image()") ximage(m, main = "ximage()") par(op) image(t(m[nrow(m):1, ]))

what: From pixel stream to matrix and back
title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: Spatial readers hand scan lines: vector values raster order, dimensions declared alongside (ncol, nrow) - x y, image-format convention. two conversions : ximage() applies conversion given reader output directly. list dimension extent attributes (vapour convention), vector list gis attribute (gdalraster convention), plots correctly handling :  rule inside ximage simple: dimensions arrived attribute, data raster-order stream gets byrow treatment; bare R matrix taken already oriented. ximage(list(volcano)) ximage(volcano) identical, reader output - even reader pre-shaped matrix - reassembled stream.
code: vals <- 1:12                # the pixel stream, raster order dimension <- c(4L, 3L)      # (ncol, nrow), as a reader declares it  m <- matrix(vals, dimension[2L], byrow = TRUE) m #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    1    2    3    4 #> [2,]    5    6    7    8 #> [3,]    9   10   11   12  ## and back again all(as.vector(t(m)) == vals) #> [1] TRUE l <- structure(list(vals), dimension = dimension, extent = c(0, 4, 0, 3)) ximage(l) xtext(l, add = TRUE)

title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: byrow array(), raster-order stream RGB bands needs one step. Band-sequential data (band 1, band 2, band 3, GDAL readers return) becomes display-ready array :  array() call shapes band (ncol, nrow) - filled column-major, column holds scan line - aperm() swaps first two dimensions give R display orientation. , ximage bands come reader-output list; recipe shown meet raw stream.
code: nbands <- 3L stream <- runif(prod(dimension) * nbands)  a <- aperm(array(stream, c(dimension[1:2], nbands)), c(2, 1, 3)) dim(a)  ## (nrow, ncol, nbands) #> [1] 3 4 3 ximage(a)

title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: extent argument (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) declares outer edges data, centres corner cells. default index-space extent c(0, ncol, 0, nrow) follows rule: cell [1, 1] spans x 0 1 y nrow - 1 nrow, centre - xtext() puts label - (0.5, nrow - 0.5).  edge convention shared GDAL geotransforms rasterImage(), makes images different sources overlay exactly: extent statement data sits, first sample taken. xcontour() uses matching cell-centre positions, contour lines image cells register correctly:
code: ximage(m, extent = c(140, 148, -44, -38)) xtext(m, extent = c(140, 148, -44, -38), add = TRUE) axis(1); axis(2) abline(v = seq(140, 148, by = 2), h = seq(-44, -38, by = 2), lty = 3) ximage(volcano) xcontour(volcano, add = TRUE, col = "white")

title: Array orientation: raster order and the R matrix
text: ximage displays matrices raster order: first cell top-left, rows scan lines. Stream matrix: matrix(vals, nrow, byrow = TRUE). Matrix stream: .vector(t(m)). Reader dimensions (ncol, nrow); R dimensions (nrow, ncol). Multi-band streams: aperm(array(vals, c(ncol, nrow, nbands)), c(2, 1, 3)). extent declares cell edges, cell centres sit half cell . ximage applies automatically vapour gdalraster output; recipes everything else.

what: ximage - draw images of raster data
title: ximage - draw images of raster data
text: goal ximage like ‘image()’ ‘rasterImage()’ missing functionality usability problems fixed. Draw image whatever , want , dependencies beyond base R. ximage supports making images numeric, character, byte matrix numeric array (including RGB/, grey/alpha) nativeRaster data returned vapour::gdal_raster_() gdalraster::read_ds() functions include numeric, character, byte vectors nativeRaster types Missing values display colour choosing (na.col, transparent default), constant alpha can applied input overlay work, zlim anchors absolute colours across multiple plots. Alongside ximage() matching adornment functions share layout conventions: xcontour() (contours cell centres), xtext() (cell values labels), xrect() (rectangles extents). orientation “raster order”, .e. ’re looking picture ’s top left top right, scan lines row bottom (like western reading par(mfrow) order). orientation explored orientation vignette. matches way spatial data readers read imagery, equivalent populating R matrix matrix(<>, nrow, ncol, byrow = TRUE) (note backwards order nrow,ncol). Please note getting data matrix order, .vector(t(m)). Higher dimensional arrays need care, ’s byrow array(). full story package vignette: vignette("orientation", package = "ximage").

title: ximage - draw images of raster data
text: basic example shows image topographic dataset, arbitrary image overlay placement.    Missing values constant transparency first-class: ocean set missing displays na.col, RGB overlay applied constant alpha.  can get imagery internet, plot quickly.
code: library(ximage) ximage(topo)  ## plot in the index space of the matrix ## or, plot in the geographic space (we happen to know this for this matrix) ximage(topo, extent = c(-180, 180, -90, 90), axes = FALSE) ximage(logo_a, extent = c(170, 180, -40, -30), add = TRUE)  axis(1); axis(2); box() ximage(logo_a)  ## plot a RGB array, a new plot in its own index space ## overlay a native raster, and a matrix with its own palette ximage(logo_n, extent = c(10, 20, 20, 40), add = TRUE) ximage(topo, extent = c(40, 60, 30, 50), add = TRUE, col = hcl.colors(256)) land <- topo land[land < 0] <- NA ximage(topo, extent = c(-180, 180, -90, 90), col = hcl.colors(64, "Blues 3")) ximage(land, extent = c(-180, 180, -90, 90), add = TRUE,        col = hcl.colors(64, "Terrain 2")) ximage(logo_a, extent = c(-60, 60, -80, -35), add = TRUE, alpha = 0.5) library(vapour)   virtual_earth <-  "<GDAL_WMS><Service name=\"VirtualEarth\"><ServerUrl>http://a${server_num}.ortho.tiles.virtualearth.net/tiles/a${quadkey}.jpeg?g=90</ServerUrl></Service><MaxConnections>4</MaxConnections><Cache/></GDAL_WMS>" par(mar = rep(0, 4)) px <- dev.size("px") px[which.min(px)] <- 0  ## zero means GDAL fills this dimension, preserving aspect  ## change lon_0 and lat_0 to anywhere you like im <- gdal_raster_nara(virtual_earth, target_ext = c(-1, 1, -1, 1) * 3e5, target_dim = px, target_crs = "+proj=laea +lon_0=147 +lat_0=-42")  system.time(ximage(im, asp = 1)) #>    user  system elapsed  #>   0.004   0.000   0.003   ## crank up the size it's still fast px <- px * 4 im <- gdal_raster_nara(virtual_earth, target_ext = c(-1, 1, -1, 1) * 3e5, target_dim = px, target_crs = "+proj=laea +lon_0=147 +lat_0=-42")  system.time(ximage(im, asp = 1)) #>    user  system elapsed  #>   0.046   0.018   0.065

title: ximage 0.1.0
text: New function xtext() draws matrix values labels cell centres, raster-order layout used ximage() (thanks draft issue #22). Supports vapour gdalraster reader-output lists. New vignette “Array orientation: raster order R matrix” explains raster-order convention, byrow = TRUE .vector(t(m)) round trip, multi-band aperm() recipes, cell-edge extent convention (#14). Now support raw output fastpng. Now support {gdalraster} output read_ds(, as_list = TRUE) raw numeric, thanks Chris Toney. ximage() now handles breaks argument go col (numeric input). image() now works list output gdalnara (gdal_raster_image nativeRaster). Added suport xcontour() output output gdal_raster_data() {vapour}. ximage() can now plot sf::gdal_read objects. Fixed default extent array/matrix, transposed (!). ximage now imfun whatarelief , .e. output gdal_raster_data, gdal_raster_dsn, gdal_raster_image obvious plot. Add ‘mesh_plot’ mode ximage(), fully implemented. Increase default colour classes, 12 -> 96. Support ‘raster’ class per .raster. Added xcontour xrect functions.
